claims.text: Carefully balanced Cr and Al contents synergistically promote simultaneous formation of a dual oxide scale in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed dual oxide scale consists predominantly of Al2O3 and Cr2O3.
The dual oxide scale adheres better than scales dominated by a single oxide former.
The dual oxide scale grows more slowly than single-oxide scales.
Improved scale adhesion and slower scale growth enhance high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Variants of AlxCrCoFeNi can be prepared with uniform microstructures and controlled Cr/Al ratios while retaining high configurational entropy.
A controlled comparison can systematically vary the Cr/Al ratio while holding the other alloying components constant.
The proposed oxidation tests cover 950–1050 °C, controlled oxygen partial pressures, and both isothermal and cyclic thermal regimes.
Interfacial interaction between Al2O3 and Cr2O3 governs scale adherence, stability, and oxidation resistance.
Cr modulates nucleation of the protective Al2O3 layer by facilitating dual-oxide formation.
Cr modulates the growth kinetics of the protective Al2O3 layer.
Cr improves adhesion of the protective Al2O3 layer.
The composite Al2O3–Cr2O3 scale impedes oxygen diffusion more effectively than a scale formed from one dominant oxide-forming element.
The composite Al2O3–Cr2O3 scale resists spallation better than a scale formed from one dominant oxide-forming element.
Balanced-Cr/Al HEAs will form thinner oxide scales than single-dominant-oxide-former HEAs under identical tests.
Balanced-Cr/Al HEAs will show lower oxidation weight gain than the baseline under identical tests.
Balanced-Cr/Al HEAs will show less scale spallation than the baseline under identical tests.
HEAs with either Al or Cr as the single dominant oxide former typically develop thicker, less adherent oxide scales under the same high-temperature conditions.
The proposed mechanism is bounded to high-configurational-entropy alloys oxidized at 950–1050 °C under controlled oxygen partial pressures.

Failure to obtain a thinner, more adherent dual-oxide scale with superior oxidation resistance, or observation of significant brittle spinel formation or accelerated oxidation, would falsify the hypothesis.
